fix: Implement the 2026-10-11 small-sample standard (RECIPES §4.6) as the below-300 standard candidate in turbotab/core/models/boosted_trees.py:71 (100 trees, <=8 leaves, lr 0.02, leaf 20, L2 1) and turbotab/core/models/xgboost_family.py:502 (depth 3, lr 0.02, child weight 20 rows-equivalent, lambda 1), update the methods sentence at boosted_trees.py:289, and replace the bit-for-bit pin in test_boosted_trees_tuned.py::test_below_300_the_tuned_fit_is_a_direct_default_fit with a held-out check against nested tuning.
evidence: tuning.py:92 (SMALL_N=300) sets S=0 so boosted trees and XGBoost are delivered at the library defaults below n_plan 300; both referees' simulations (calibration slopes 0.2-0.5, log loss worse in every data set) and the repo's own SMALL_SAMPLE_STANDARD.md §2 (defaults the worst arm in all 14 cells, regret 0.10-0.39 nats, slope ~0.3) refute 'at least as well and better calibrated'. I accept the audit: the cited Riley/Van Calster/Martin papers concern penalized regression, and the ruled fix is not built, so every small-table boosted fit is overconfident and loses model comparisons.

fix: In turbotab/core/models/selection.py:1000 and the verdict at ~1086, replace NO_COST with an absence-of-evidence wording (e.g. 'these rows cannot tell the two apart; the interval spans 0'), label the interval as BBC-CV's percentile interval of out-of-bag estimates (conservative, per Tsamardinos et al. 2018) rather than a plain '95% interval', and raise the calibration clause's floor above n >= 10 (e.g. require a minimum count of out-of-bag events per resample before reporting |1 - slope|).
evidence: The procedure is BBC-CV as published (both referees and the audit agree; the pick is re-made per resample at selection.py:1048-1052), so the selection correction itself stands. But my simulation (3 equal flexible families, fixed OOF losses) gives the percentile interval ~99.5% coverage, and it spans 0 in 19% of n=100 cases with a real cost versus 5% for a calibrated paired 95% interval, confirming Referee A that 'no measurable cost' fires too often and tilts toward the interpretable model; Referee B's point that an interval spanning 0 is not evidence of no cost also holds. The shown interval keeps this a wording/regime fix rather than a wrong number, and the calibration slope on ~4 out-of-bag rows at the 10-row floor is rarely reached.

fix: Correct the inventory statement to the audit's version: Riley's minimum is computed only for numeric and yes/no outcomes (selection.py:959-964 says so for others) and not at all under inference (selection.py:946-947); the smallest-class count is only the effective size for Harrell's knot count (modeling.py:163-166), not Riley's events.
evidence: Referee A's only objection (the smallest-class shortcut is not Pate et al.'s multinomial criterion) does not apply: shelf_order calls prediction_minimum, which handles only 'regression' and 'binary' (sample_size.py:175-209), so a multiclass outcome gets no Riley minimum and the shelf says so; under inference shelf_order returns before computing one and rule_spline_terms returns 0. The parameter counting itself (k-1 per category, every spline/quintile column, k-2 per bendable predictor) matches Riley et al. 2020/2019 as Referee B and the audit found, and is checked against pmsampsize and hand counts in test_explore_repair.py::test_5 and test_wp8_inference_reporting.py::test_4a/4c.

fix: Reword the band-0 reason at turbotab/core/materiality.py:1034-1036 from 'That is below what would move the estimate' to a hedged prediction ('expected to move it little; checked after the plan is fixed'), and set rows_smd 'calibrated' to false in turbotab/core/materiality_calibration.json:15 until it is calibrated per SURFACING_POLICY §2.6 (reference journeys, cry-wolf budget, held-out cases), ideally adding the pure sampling movement SE*sqrt(s/(1-s)) of dropping a share s to the predicted band.
evidence: The 0.003697 cut is the m_pre of the smallest falsely reassured case among 9 in-sample cases from one fixture with a single band-0 case (audit), and the proxy cannot guarantee the stated bound: dropping a share s of rows moves the estimate by SE*sqrt(s/(1-s)) from sampling alone (Referee A; at s = 3.7% that is already ~0.1 half-width SD), and the half-width shrinks with n while a fixed share x SMD shift does not (Referee B). I treat it as S2 rather than S1 because the sensitivity stage adds Banna's every-row analysis automatically and verify() (materiality.py:1086-1102) relabels an upgraded movement openly and drafts a limitation, so the reported numbers are corrected after the lock in the common single-screen case.

fix: Reword residual_label at turbotab/core/methods/exposure_form.py:975-981 to say the residual curve is the fixed-energy curve at mean energy under a structure in which the curve shifts with energy along N - b(E - mean E), that the standard model spline(N) + E instead assumes one curve at every energy, that the two agree only for a straight line, and that the standard model is the route to the conventional (energy-invariant) substitution curve, not the only definition of one.
evidence: The straight-line identity and the 'energy-adjusted scale at mean energy' wording are right (Referee B, audit; the residual is N - b(E - mean E)). But algebra settles the referees' split in A's favor on one phrase: at E = mean E the residual is N itself, so the residual model's plotted curve is that model's own curve in N at fixed total energy (mean energy), and each model recovers the fixed-energy curve only under its own structure (Referee A's simulation; B's simulation used an additive truth). So 'not the substitution curve at fixed total energy' states the additive assumption as a definition; offering the standard model is the conventional, defensible route, which makes this a wording fix.

fix: In turbotab/core/methods/trials.py:715-751, stop refusing the standardized risk difference under separation: compute the arm risks from the fitted limit (or a Firth-penalized fit, or with the separated stratum collapsed), report the RD always and the RR when both arms' standardized risks are positive, use an interval that survives separation (Firth/profile or a bootstrap), and change the message to 'the logistic model's coefficients have no finite values' instead of 'no finite estimate exists'; distinguish the |beta| > 25 / risk < 1e-10 triggers from true separation.
evidence: Both referees and the audit agree, and Referee A's simulation shows it: under separation only the coefficients diverge, while the g-computed arm risks are averages of bounded fitted risks with finite limits, so the RD (and usually the RR) exists. The app refuses the trial's pre-specified adjusted effect for that false reason, and its only exit drops every covariate (covariates: []); with zero events in one arm (common for rare outcomes) even the unadjusted fit separates and no RD is given at all, although it is finite (e.g. 0/50 vs 20/50 = 0.40).

fix: Mark MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 1(c) and §2's change-in-estimate rung as doc-only (not built) in the claims ledger, or, if change-in-estimate is ever offered, implement the block-and-record label with the VanderWeele 2019 reason; no code change is needed while no such option exists.
evidence: Both referees judge the statement true and the audit verified VanderWeele 2019 ('inappropriate for non-collapsible measures such as the odds ratio or hazard ratio if the outcome is common'); test_estimand_1_effect_measure.py::test_1 certifies only the non-collapsibility premise. A grep of turbotab/ and turbotab/frontend/src finds change-in-estimate only in that test's docstring, so the claimed block-and-record label does not exist; since the app offers no change-in-estimate selection either, no user is exposed and the gap is ledger hygiene.

fix: In turbotab/core/stages/modeling.py:1014-1018 name the default correctly and as a convention ('the median observed time, event or censoring, of the training rows: a convention, as no prediction horizon was declared') or switch to the reverse-Kaplan-Meier median, and expose FollowUpSpec.prediction_horizon (decisions.py:941) in the follow-up card so a clinical horizon can be declared.
evidence: Both referees find no methods basis for the median as an 'appropriate' horizon and the audit confirms the contract (validation.py:990-1010) records a decision without a reason; McLernon et al. 2023 ties the horizon to the clinical question. The behavior is defensible as a fallback (half the training rows remain at risk at that time, which keeps IPCW stable), but the text calls np.median of event-or-censoring times 'the median follow-up time', which is shorter than the reverse-KM median follow-up epidemiologists mean, and no UI control sets prediction_horizon, so this unlabeled default governs every time-to-event Brier score and calibration.

fix: Correct the inventory: name-blind contiguous-block batch candidates are appended after the named batch/run/plate columns (not only when none is named) and can fill the second slot, and the level cap is max(2, n//4) (turbotab/core/readings.py:3195-3216); optionally add a unit test that calls injection_order_reading and batch_readings on the permutation, block and cap cases, which no test does now.
evidence: Both referees judge the claim true: injection order and analytical batch are run properties that values cannot identify, and a name-plus-structure guess settled by the user (KIND_RULES, the 'one curve over the whole run' option always offered) is the right design. The only discrepancies are the audit's two detail errors in the inventory ('else' vs 'then' for block candidates; n/4 vs max(2, n//4)), which I confirmed in batch_readings; the app's own docstring describes the code correctly, and the caps are interface conventions that cannot mislead because the user chooses.

fix: No change to the QRILC refusal (turbotab/core/methods/omics.py:1471-1478); separately, the half-minimum path (omics.py:1480-1492) should say that a single fill also leaves the imputation uncertainty out of the intervals, which belongs to the half-minimum claim, not this one.
evidence: Both referees confirm the reason (a single completed draw treated as observed drops the between-imputation variance; Referee A's simulation shows 84-92% coverage at 30-50% censored), and the refusal routes to the censored-normal draw within the multiple imputation, a sound estimate, so nothing valid is withheld. The audit's only objection is unevenness with half-minimum, which is accepted at <=10% (Lubin's customary share) or above it only when recorded as a limitation; that concerns the half-minimum rule's wording, not the correctness of this refusal.

fix: Amend docs/turbotab-next/calm/BEATS_PREDICT.md:1494 (§17 ruling 7) to match the engine and its own Table 2 (line 988-989): the opened cycle's R² is measured against the development (training) mean, per models/metrics.py and voice.py:1209-1211; if an own-mean R² is ever shown beside it, label each with its reference mean.
evidence: Both referees prove the statement true (own-mean SST <= development-mean SST, so own-mean R² is lower and is sklearn's convention), but the audit and code show the engine does the opposite: R² against the training rows' mean (Staerk et al. 2024, audit MA-09), and test_modeling.py:200-225 asserts it is not the own-mean r2_score. The engine's choice is the deployable out-of-sample R² and is labeled in the record, so the only defect is a design ruling that contradicts the built behavior, with no user exposure.

fix: Wire the metafor-checked REML + HKSJ pooling from methods/site_validation.py into validation.internal_external in place of the DerSimonian-Laird z interval in turbotab/core/models/performance.py:906-917 (INBOX T3), and before building P27 drop the identity-scale-optimism reason for the log scale (and Snell 2018 as its source) or label a back-transformed log-MSE as the typical (median) cycle's MSE, not the mean.
evidence: The ruling is unbuilt: performance.random_effects pools on the identity scale with DL tau², a normal-z CI and a t(k-2) prediction interval (audit, confirmed in code). My simulation (k = 8 cycles) shows the stated reason is wrong in the survey regime: identity-scale optimism vanishes by n = 1,000 per cycle (pooled 1.008 vs true mean 1.011), while the back-transformed log-scale estimate targets the median and sits below the mean under heterogeneity (1.006 vs 1.046), as both referees caveated. What does bite in the shipped engine is the interval: the DL z CI covered 0.87-0.91 under heterogeneity versus 0.94-0.96 for HKSJ, so the user's pooled interval is modestly too narrow today.
